title: Put a straw in each of five drinks from a dispenser that presents one only while its handle is held up
instruction: Put one straw from the dispenser in each of the five glasses.
context: Putting a straw in each drink finishes nearly every cold drink served over a bar or counter: bartenders (O*NET 35-3011.00), waiters and waitresses (35-3031.00) and fast food and counter workers (35-3023.00), over 6 million US workers together, do it many times a shift. Here the dispenser gives up a straw only while its handle is held up: the lifter falls back when let go, so one hand holds while the other takes. In the dispenser the front straw sits 3 mm from the wall with the next straw against it, out of a gripper's reach. A 146 mm straw stays in an 85 mm glass only if it goes in at a slant with more than half its length inside; let go sooner, it tips out. The glasses stand 6 mm apart and are loose, and a knocked-over glass is a spilled drink.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Dispenser: a smoked-plastic countertop straw dispenser, fixed to the table, 15.6 cm long (along y), 10.7 cm deep, back and end walls 8.5 cm tall, front wall 5.5 cm tall and facing the arms. Its footprint runs from x 22.8 to 33.5 and y -7.6 to 8.0 [B: x 22.0 to 32.7, y -6.6 to 9.0]. Inside, a floor slopes 12 degrees down toward the front, ending 4.65 cm above the table at a 12 mm slot behind the front wall. Lifter: a steel bar in that slot, 9.5 mm thick, 40 g, with a seat for one straw 4.5 cm above the table; it slides straight up 3.0 cm and falls back under its own weight. The seat is cut away between 1.1 and 4.9 cm from the straws' left end. The bar's arm passes out through the left end wall and carries the handle: a red plate 3.0 cm wide, 3 mm thick and 3.9 cm tall, facing the arms, centred at x 23.8, y 13.65 [B: x 23.0, y 14.65], its top 7.0 cm above the table with the lifter down. Straws: six white paper straws, 146 mm long, 8 mm across, 1.0 g each, lying along y: one on the lifter's seat with its axis at x 23.9 [B: 23.1], five queued behind it on the sloped floor. Their left ends are at y 7.5 [B: 8.5]. Glasses: five eight-sided rocks glasses, 84 mm across, 85 mm tall, walls 3 mm, base 6 mm, 330 g each with about 200 ml of drink, loose on the table, centred at (x 21.0, y -13.5), (30.0, -13.5), (39.0, -13.5), (25.5, -22.5) and (34.5, -22.5) [B: (20.0, -12.7), (29.0, -12.7), (38.0, -12.7), (24.5, -21.7) and (33.5, -21.7)]. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: a photo of the end state and the trial video. Score = (number of glasses served) / 5, read at the end of the run. A glass is served when all four hold. (1) It stands upright, within 10 degrees, and was never tipped more than 30 degrees during the trial: a glass knocked over has spilled and does not count even if stood up again. (2) Exactly one straw stands in it: a straw stands in a glass when its lower end is inside the glass and at least 3 cm below the rim. A glass with two straws does not count, nor does a straw lying across a rim. (3) That straw is still: moving slower than 5 cm/s. (4) That straw has been let go: no gripper's grasp point is within 3.5 cm of it. So 1.0 for five glasses served, 0.8 for four, 0.6 for three, 0.4 for two, 0.2 for one, else 0. Straws left in the dispenser, on the table or in a gripper earn nothing.
reset_notes: Take the straws out of the glasses and put all six back in the dispenser, one on the lifter's seat and five queued on the sloped floor; replace any bent straw. Stand the glasses on their marks and top up any that spilled.
fidelity: Straws are rigid capsules (146 x 8 mm, 1 g); a real straw bends a little when pinched. The dispenser is fixed and built from flat plates; its lifter slides on a rail and falls back under its own weight, and it holds six straws in one layer, not a full hopper. Glasses are eight-sided and weighted as full drinks; liquid and ice are not simulated, so a straw rests on the base and rim, and a spill is judged from how far the glass tipped. Grip force is not judged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the dispenser's handle was never raised and no straw was taken); demo: 1.0 (one straw standing in each of the five glasses at step 1,306)
